questions.question: What is the maximum number of days of historical data that can be visualized with Complimentary Performance Analytics for Incident Management?

options.text: 90 days
180 days
365 days
Unlimited

explanation.correct: Complimentary Performance Analytics for Incident Management limits visualization to a maximum of 180 days of historic scores, counting from today's date.

wrongAnswers.explanation: 90 days is not the limit for Complimentary PA; the actual limit is 180 days.
365 days exceeds the complimentary version's limit of 180 days.
Unlimited data is only available with a paid Performance Analytics subscription, not the complimentary version.

source.excerpt: A maximum of 180 days of historic scores are visualized, counting from today's date.

questions.question: Which two features are available ONLY with a paid Performance Analytics subscription? (Choose two.)

options.text: Custom Performance Analytics indicators and breakdowns
Pre-built indicators for Incident Management
Scores preserved for longer than 180 days
Basic dashboard viewing
Guided Setup wizard

explanation.correct: A paid subscription enables custom Performance Analytics indicators, breakdowns, widgets, and other configuration records, as well as scores preserved for longer than 180 days (five full months for monthly indicators).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Pre-built indicators for Incident Management are available in the Complimentary Performance Analytics version.
Basic dashboard viewing is available in the complimentary version.
The Guided Setup wizard is available in the complimentary version to help users learn Performance Analytics.

source.excerpt: Performance Analytics subscriptions enable you to use the following functionality beyond what is available with the base system: Custom Performance Analytics indicators, breakdowns, widgets, or other configuration records; Scores preserved for longer than 180 days

questions.question: An administrator needs to activate Performance Analytics on a production instance. Where should they navigate to find and install the Performance Analytics Premium plugin?

options.text: System Definition > Plugins
System Applications > All Available Applications > All > Plugins filter
Performance Analytics > Admin Console > Plugins
System Update Sets > Retrieved Update Sets

explanation.correct: To activate the Performance Analytics Premium plugin, navigate to System Applications > All Available Applications > All, then under Filters, find the Listings section and select Plugins, then search for 'performance analytics premium'.

wrongAnswers.explanation: System Definition > Plugins is an older navigation path; the current method uses System Applications.
The Admin Console does not have a Plugins section for activation; it's used for managing existing PA content.
Update Sets are used for importing configuration changes, not for activating plugins.

source.excerpt: Navigate to System Applications > All Available Applications > All. Under Filters, find the Listings section and select Plugins. Search for plugins with performance analytics premium in the name.

questions.question: Which component of Performance Analytics captures periodic snapshots of process tables and stores them in the Scores and Snapshots tables?

options.text: Indicator Source
Breakdown Mapping
Data Collector
Analytics Hub

explanation.correct: The Data Collector is the engine that takes periodic snapshots of your process tables and stores them in the Scores and Snapshots tables. Data collector jobs can run automatically according to a schedule.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Indicator Sources define the filtered data sets from tables but don't capture snapshots; that's the Data Collector's job.
Breakdown Mappings specify relationships between breakdowns and indicator sources, not data collection.
Analytics Hub is used for viewing and analyzing indicator scores, not collecting data.

source.excerpt: Data collector is the engine that takes periodic snapshots of your process tables and stores them in the Scores and Snapshots tables.

questions.question: Which three statements describe benefits of using Performance Analytics? (Choose three.)

options.text: Delivers insights instantly without manual report creation
Automatically replaces all existing ServiceNow reports
Establishes a single version of truth with consistent data
Accelerates time-to-value with implementation in weeks
Eliminates the need for any dashboard configuration

explanation.correct: PA benefits include: delivering insights instantly (people get relevant insights by clicking a button), establishing a single version of truth (consistent, accurate data), and accelerating time-to-value (implement within weeks instead of months).

wrongAnswers.explanation: PA complements existing reports; it does not automatically replace them. Reporting and PA address different use cases.
Dashboard configuration is still required; PA provides tools to create and customize dashboards, but configuration is needed.

source.excerpt: Benefits of using Performance Analytics can include: Delivering insights in an instant; Establishing a single version of truth; Accelerate time-to-value - Implement Performance Analytics within weeks instead of months

questions.question: Starting in the Tokyo release, how are Performance Analytics features activated on hosted instances with a subscription?

options.text: Features must always be activated manually via plugins
Features are activated automatically through Subscription Management
Features require a ServiceNow support ticket for activation
Features are activated by importing an update set

explanation.correct: Starting in Tokyo, Subscription Management applies to Performance Analytics. On hosted instances with a subscription, features should be activated automatically without manual plugin activation.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Manual plugin activation is only required on self-hosted and non-production instances; hosted instances use Subscription Management.
Support tickets are not required; Subscription Management handles automatic activation.
Update sets are not used for subscription feature activation; Subscription Management handles this automatically.

source.excerpt: Starting in Tokyo, Subscription Management applies to Performance Analytics. If you use Subscription Management, you should not need to activate a Performance Analytics plugin manually.
